svg.title: the devil is in the details

text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/10/31 - Idioms & slang - 01

svg.title: Small print can contain a condition that changes the whole plan.

text.tspan: Small print can contain a condition that changes the whole plan.
the devil is in the details
A plan that appears straightforward may depend on small, easily
overlooked details.
small points can cause big problems; careful execution matters
The costume contest sounded open to everyone, but the devil was
in the details: entrants needed to register before noon.
Often used as a warning after broad agreement with a proposal. It
draws attention to implementation; it does not mean every plan is
doomed.
A: Entry is free, so we can register when we get there.
B: Read the small print. Registration closes at noon.
A: Ah, the devil is in the details. I only noticed “free entry.”
B: We still have twenty minutes. Let’s register now.
Which overlooked detail best justifies this idiom? A: The poster is
orange. B: Registration closes six hours before the contest. C: The
event has a cheerful name. Give one practical consequence.
(Model: B. Someone arriving at the contest without registering
earlier could be unable to enter, even though admission is free.)
